paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minADE₂₀ (lower is better) as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis represents the "Number of Examples," displayed on a linear scale from 0 to 8 with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis represents "minADE₂₀ (←)", also on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.128 to 0.14, with tick marks at 0.13 and 0.14 (note that the axis appears to have a label misalignment: values above 0.13 are labeled as 0.13, but visually they correspond to higher values; the actual values decrease downward, which is unconventional). The ST-ES method starts at approximately 0.139 when the number of examples is 0, drops sharply to around 0.132 at 2 examples, dips further to approximately 0.130 at 4 examples, and then remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations, ending near 0.131 at 8 examples. The Random method begins at 0.140, drops to approximately 0.132 at 1 example, remains flat around 0.132 to 0.133 until 4 examples, then increases to about 0.138 at 6 examples before rising further to 0.140 at 8 examples. Both lines show variability, but ST-ES maintains lower and more stable minADE₂₀ values across the range compared to Random.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minADE₂₀ as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at intervals of 2, ranging from 0 to 8. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (←)", is also linearly scaled, ranging approximately from 0.128 to 0.14, with tick marks at 0.13, 0.135, and 0.14. The ST-ES method starts at a minADE₂₀ of approximately 0.139 at 0 examples and decreases to about 0.129 at 4 examples, then remains relatively stable, fluctuating slightly between 0.129 and 0.131 up to 8 examples. The Random method begins at a minADE₂₀ of approximately 0.14 at 0 examples, drops to about 0.13 at 2 examples, remains relatively flat until 6 examples, then dips to approximately 0.128 at 6 examples before rising to about 0.138 at 8 examples. Both lines are solid, with markers at each data point, and the plot includes a legend in the upper right corner indicating the two methods.
